events.title: Justinian lays the foundation of the Hagia Sophia
events.description: Byzantine emperor Justinian I laid the foundation stone of a new Orthodox Christian basilica in Constantinople. It replaced an earlier church that had been destroyed in the Nika riots, and it became the Hagia Sophia.
events.significance: The Hagia Sophia became one of the great landmarks of world architecture. Its vast dome influenced church and mosque design for centuries.

events.title: Traditional date of the Gutenberg Bible's publication
events.description: February 23 is the traditional date given for the publication of the Gutenberg Bible. It was the first major Western book printed with movable metal type.
events.significance: Movable-type printing spread knowledge across Europe much faster than hand copying could. It helped drive the Renaissance, the Reformation and the Scientific Revolution.

events.title: Cuba leases Guantánamo Bay to the United States
events.description: Cuba leased Guantánamo Bay to the United States "in perpetuity". The agreement gave the US a naval station on the island's southeastern coast.
events.significance: The base is still a point of dispute between the two countries. It later became internationally known as a detention site.

events.title: Flag raised on Mount Suribachi at Iwo Jima
events.description: During the Battle of Iwo Jima, a group of US Marines reached the top of Mount Suribachi and raised the American flag. The moment was photographed.
events.significance: The photograph won a Pulitzer Prize and became one of the best-known images of World War II. It inspired the Marine Corps War Memorial.
